answer: The split tally binds one newcomer to one climb. At the summit muster a newcomer locks a $5 bond and takes one timber tally marked with yarrow dye; the climb must end before the bell, where the keeper splits it and keeps one half. The keeper fits the halves together and checks the dye mark in the log within the hour; a half that will not fit or a copied mark burns the bond. One climber spends $5; faking a hundred costs a hundred climbs and $500.
